meta.description: Machine-persistable reference mapping linking ESG research objectives to literature evidence and causal logic chains.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?

RQ1.1 (v1): How can we design a Document-, Tone-, and Ontology-Aware ESG-ABSA system?

literature_references.title: Translation between typologically diverse languages
literature_references.relevance: Provides the linguistic theoretical basis for managing cross-lingual transfer (C3) between typologically distinct languages, essential for Indonesian-English ESG alignment (RQ1.1).

literature_references.title: AFRIDOC-MT: Document-level MT Corpus for African Languages
literature_references.relevance: Demonstrates the necessity of document-level datasets (C9) and the challenges of generalizing from sentence-level to longer document contexts (RQ1.1v1).

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: Demystifying Domain-adaptive Post-training for Financial LLMs
literature_references.relevance: Directly supports the large-scale benchmarking of LLMs for financial tasks (C8) and evaluates domain adaptation strategies required for ESG granularity (RQ2.1).

literature_references.title: CoLA: Compute-Efficient Pre-Training of LLMs via Low-Rank Activation
literature_references.relevance: Validates the use of low-rank activations to enhance training efficiency and representation scalability (C13), addressing long-context limitations (RQ2.2).

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can explainable AI enhance stakeholder trust?
RQ3.1 (v1): How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?

literature_references.title: ReAgent: Reversible Multi-Agent Reasoning for Knowledge-Enhanced Multi-Hop QA
literature_references.relevance: Introduces backtracking mechanisms in multi-agent reasoning, supporting the transparent outputs required for GraphRAG architectures (C7, RQ3.2).

literature_references.title: Towards Statistical Factuality Guarantee for Large Vision-Language Models
literature_references.relevance: Provides a framework for claim verification and statistical guarantees on output factuality, directly linked to enhancing stakeholder trust (C4, RQ3.1).

research_questions: RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?

literature_references.title: Graders should cheat: privileged information enables expert-level automated evaluations
literature_references.relevance: Uses ground-truth guidelines to improve automated evaluations, supporting the development of ontology-linked metrics for detecting credibility risks (C6, RQ4.2).

literature_references.title: Unveiling the Response of Large Vision-Language Models to Visually Absent Tokens
literature_references.relevance: Investigates model responses to absent or mismatched evidence, providing a methodology for quantifying tone-action-outcome mismatches in greenwashing (C11, RQ4.5).

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: Model-based Large Language Model Customization as Service
literature_references.relevance: Discusses the deployment of customized LLMs as a service, supporting the operationalization of a production-grade ESG platform (C1, RQ5.2).

literature_references.title: BannerAgency: Advertising Banner Design with Multimodal LLM Agents
literature_references.relevance: Demonstrates the use of blueprints and editable components (SVG) for visual interfaces, informing the design of auditable ESG dashboards (C12, RQ5.1).
